_doc: Water-safety limits: TMV outlet temperatures and dead-leg lengths. The ONE owner of these values (DSCH-25);
read by Core/Plumbing/WaterSafetyLimits.cs (TMVEngine, WaterSafetyValidator, DeadLegDetector). No code constant
backs them: a missing or invalid file makes every check report NOT CHECKED.
TMV schemes: TMV2 = BS EN 1111 / BS EN 1287 (TMV2 scheme, domestic); TMV3 = NHS D08 (healthcare). The previous
'BS 8680 classes A/B/C' were not a real classification and are removed.
maxSetC = maximum set delivery temperature; neverExceedC = highest acceptable measured outlet temperature.
A row with a 'verify' text is not confirmed against the primary standard: confirm it before relying on it. Rows without one cite the primary document (DSCH-41).
Approved Document G G3(4) caps a bath in a new dwelling in England at 48 C; the 44 C rows below are stricter and govern.
jurisdiction: rows without it are HTM 04-01 (England) and apply wherever a region has no row of its own for that outlet and scheme;
SCOTLAND rows (SHTM 04-01 Part A v2, July 2014, Table 4) apply when PRJ_ORG_HEALTH_HTM_REGION_TXT names Scotland (DSCH-36).
An unrecorded region keeps the England rows and the check says so.
Wales and Northern Ireland have no rows of their own yet.
SHTM Table 4 also gives 'Office, staff-only access areas hand-wash basins 43 C, Type 1' — a Type 1 device is not a TMV scheme here, so it has no row.
healthcareRequiredSchemeSource: HTM 04-01 Part A (2016) Table 2; HSG274 Part 2 §2.76 (type 3 valves required at healthcare premises)

outletLimits.source: HTM 04-01 Part A (2016) Table 2 — unassisted baths 44 °C; never-exceed = set + 2 °C per HTM 04-01 Supplement, Performance specification D 08: thermostatic mixing valves (healthcare premises), 2017 edition, Table 17 note ('the mixed water temperature can deviate by 2 °C from these maximum initial settings') and §11.1.2.5 / §11.2.2.4 (commissioning and in-service tests: no more than 2 °C from the set temperature), https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Health_tech_memo_0401_supp_D08.pdf

HTM 04-01 Part A (2016) Table 2 — baths for assisted bathing 46 °C (cold mass of the bath); exceptional circumstances only, water checked with a thermometer before immersion; never-exceed = set + 2 °C per HTM 04-01 Supplement, Performance specification D 08: thermostatic mixing valves (healthcare premises), 2017 edition, Table 17 note ('the mixed water temperature can deviate by 2 °C from these maximum initial settings') and §11.1.2.5 / §11.2.2.4 (commissioning and in-service tests: no more than 2 °C from the set temperature), https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Health_tech_memo_0401_supp_D08.pdf
outletLimits.note: Use only where the Water Safety Group has approved assisted bathing above 44 °C with a safe means of preventing access

outletLimits.source: SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (July 2014) Table 4 'Safe water temperatures and delivery devices' — general baths 43 °C, Type 3 thermostatic; never-exceed = Table 4 + 2 °C per SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (July 2014) §16 'Temperature testing' (p. 95): 'the maximum temperatures should not exceed those shown in Table 4 by more than 2 °C'; Type 3 valves to MES D08 (§9.52), https://www.nss.nhs.scot/media/1806/shtm-04-01-part-a-v20-jul-2014.pdf

SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (July 2014) Table 4 'Safe water temperatures and delivery devices' — assisted baths 46 °C to allow for the cold mass of the bath; nurses should always use a thermometer before immersing patients; never-exceed = Table 4 + 2 °C per SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (July 2014) §16 'Temperature testing' (p. 95): 'the maximum temperatures should not exceed those shown in Table 4 by more than 2 °C'; Type 3 valves to MES D08 (§9.52), https://www.nss.nhs.scot/media/1806/shtm-04-01-part-a-v20-jul-2014.pdf

SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (July 2014) Table 4 'Safe water temperatures and delivery devices' — paediatric baths 40 °C to allow for the cold paediatric bath/sink; paediatric nurses should always use a thermometer; never-exceed = Table 4 + 2 °C per SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (July 2014) §16 'Temperature testing' (p. 95): 'the maximum temperatures should not exceed those shown in Table 4 by more than 2 °C'; Type 3 valves to MES D08 (§9.52), https://www.nss.nhs.scot/media/1806/shtm-04-01-part-a-v20-jul-2014.pdf
outletLimits.note: No parameter marks a bath as paediatric yet: this limit is reported NOT CHECKED when a bath is above it

deadLegLimits.governingTest: HSG274 Part 2 §2.82: hot water reaches 50 °C (55 °C in healthcare) within one minute at outlets; cold below 20 °C within two minutes. HSG274 gives no length; the lengths below are design proxies.

healthcareSpur.source: HTM 04-01 Part A (2016) §12.5 — complete spur length generally ≤ 3 m, measured on the pipe centreline from the circulating pipework or cold main to the point of discharge

blendedDownstream.source: HTM 04-01 Part A (2016) §10.48 — supply downstream of the mixing device generally ≤ 2 m (also communal blending)

deadLegLimits.uninsulatedHotSource: BS 8558:2015 Tables 6/7 (referenced by HTM 04-01 Part A §9.x) — maximum length of uninsulated hot pipe by outside diameter
deadLegLimits.uninsulatedHotVerify: values recalled from the BS 6700 Table 4 lineage, not read from BS 8558:2015 (paywalled; checked 2026-10-02: HTM 04-01 Part A (2016) and WHTM 04-01:2016 point to BS 8558 Tables 6 and 7 for the lengths but do not reproduce them, and HSG274 Part 2 gives no length) — confirm every row against BS 8558:2015 Tables 6 and 7
deadLegLimits.redundantBranchSource: industry practice for cutting back a redundant branch; HSG274 Part 2 §2.77 says only 'as close as possible' to the common supply
deadLegLimits.redundantBranchVerify: the 2 × DN figure is not in HSG274 Part 2 (§2.77: cut back as close as possible to a common supply), HTM 04-01 Part A (2016), WHTM 04-01:2016 Part A or SHTM 04-01 Part A v2 (remove redundant branches, replace tees with straight couplings) — all read 2026-10-02; confirm its source (water-fittings / BS 8558 guidance) before relying on it
